title: Reservation service core design
idea: ReservationService is a facade that holds room nights, prices them and charges payment, with each swappable rule behind its own interface.

analogy.text: A hotel front office manager asks the inventory clerk, the rate sheet and the card machine in turn. Swap the rate sheet and the manager's routine stays the same.
analogy.breaks: Code swaps a rule at construction time, not mid-shift.

points: Facade: callers see `hold` and `confirm`, never the parts behind them.
Strategy: PricingStrategy and CancellationPolicy change per rate plan without service edits.
InventoryStore reserves every night of a stay, or none of them.
A declined payment releases the nights at once, so rooms are never stranded.

steps.caption: Guest G-7 asks for a Deluxe room, check-in 13 March, check-out 15 March.
The service turns the stay into a list of nights: the 13th and the 14th.
Inventory checks both nights and takes one Deluxe unit on each.
The pricing strategy prices each night on its own, so weekend nights can cost more.
The caller gets reservation `RS-1` in HELD state, with a deadline from the injected `Clock`.
G-9 wants 14 to 16 March. The 14th has no Deluxe left, so nothing is taken.
G-7 confirms `RS-1`. The gateway charges the held total once.
Payment succeeds and `RS-1` becomes CONFIRMED. A decline would have released both nights.

code.title: Service and its policies
code.caption: One Deluxe room, two guests with overlapping stays. The service only talks to interfaces.

walk.text: Wire a fixed clock, one Deluxe room, weekend pricing and a fake gateway lambda.
G-7 holds Friday and Saturday; G-9 overlaps on Saturday and is refused.
Three interfaces: one per policy the business may want to swap.
Check every night first, then take them all, inside one lock.
Friday and Saturday nights cost 20 percent more, in integer minor units.
`hold`: nights from the range, reserve all, price each, deadline in 15 minutes.
`confirm`: refuse stale holds, charge once, release nights if the card fails.

code.title: A new cancellation plan
code.caption: Two new CancellationPolicy classes. Nothing that already exists is edited to add them.

walk.text: One paid amount, three rate plans, each with its own refund rule.
Ask each plan what it refunds at 10, 3 and 0 days before.
Tiered: full refund a week out, half from two days, then nothing.
NonRefundable always returns zero; the service handles it like any plan.

pitfalls: Do not add `if (plan == ...)` branches in the service; add a CancellationPolicy class.
Reserve inventory before charging; charging first leaves a paid guest without a room.
Release held nights on every failure path; expired holds are freed by the sweeper (page five).

quiz.q: What does CoreReservation print for G-9?
options: G-9: no DLX for those nights
quiz.why: G-9's stay includes 14 March, which RS-1 already holds. `reserve` finds zero free and returns false, so the service throws.

takeaway: A facade calls interfaces; new plans arrive as new classes, not edits.

starters: Is WeekdayWeekendPricing better as a strategy or a decorator?
Where should the hold time of 15 minutes be configured?
How do I test ReservationService without a payment gateway?
